chunks: Laying out and routing multiple decoupling capacitors. The question: If you have multiple decoupling capacitors, how do you lay them out and route them?
Many decoupling capacitors work as a team only if you arrange them well.
Put the smallest ones right against the chip's power pins, the medium ones a bit farther out, and the big ones near the power source.
Give every capacitor its own short connection to the power and ground planes, so the connections do not get in each other's way.
Think of fire stations in a city. Small stations on every block reach a fire in seconds. Bigger stations farther away carry more equipment but take longer to arrive.
If every small station had to share one narrow road, the trucks would jam.
So each station gets its own route out, and the city is laid out in tiers: fast and small near the fire, slow and big farther back.
The faster the current you must supply, the smaller the inductance you can afford between the capacitors and the chip.

Bulk capacitors at 100 kilohertz can sit at 16 nanohenries (centimetres away); capacitors serving 100 megahertz must have 16 pH, which means a large parallel array of parts with their own vias under the BGA.
Tier: a group of capacitors with similar values that covers one band of frequencies.
Loop inductance: the inductance of the path current takes from the capacitor to the chip and back ("Why decoupling must sit close to the package").
Via: a tiny plated hole that links a pad to a layer inside the board. Power and ground planes: whole copper layers that carry supply current and act as wide, low-inductance roads.
Target impedance: the most impedance the supply may show, Z target equals change in V over change in I ("Decoupling capacitors and when needed").
Say the rail must stay under 10 milliohms up to 100 megahertz. The allowed inductance is L equals Z over (2 pi f) , about 16 pH.

8 nanohenries over 16 pH equals 50 capacitors, each with its own vias, right under the chip. That is the whole idea.
"I arrange them as tiers: the smallest values against the supply pins or under the BGA balls, mid-value a bit further, bulk near the regulator.

Each capacitor gets its own power and ground via pair, side by side, to adjacent power and ground planes, with no daisy-chains or shared vias, and with neighbours' polarity alternated so fields cancel.
The planes carry current between tiers. Then I check the combined impedance against a target and damp any anti-resonance."
